title: NEB Class 11 Chemistry — Chemical Bonding And Shapes Of Molecules — 2021
origin: curated NEB-pattern set filling the 2021 gap for class-11 chemical bonding

questions.question: State the octet rule and give two limitations with examples. Why does $\mathrm{BF_3}$ violate it?
questions.solution:
Octet rule: atoms bond so as to have eight electrons in the valence shell (the noble-gas configuration).
Limitations: (1) Incomplete octet — $\mathrm{BF_3}$ has only 6 electrons around B, $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$ only 4; (2) Expanded octet — $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ (10), $\mathrm{SF_6}$ (12) using vacant d-orbitals; (3) odd-electron molecules like NO are stable with 7/11 electrons.
$\mathrm{BF_3}$: boron has 3 valence electrons and forms 3 single bonds (6 shared electrons). Adding a fourth bond is impossible without exceeding its available orbitals, so it stays electron-deficient — a strong Lewis acid.

questions.question: Using VSEPR theory, predict the shapes of $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$, and arrange their bond angles in decreasing order with justification.
questions.solution:
VSEPR: electron pairs repel; order lone-pair–lone-pair > lone-pair–bond-pair > bond-pair–bond-pair.
$\mathrm{CH_4}$: 4 bond pairs, no lone pair → tetrahedral, $109.5^\circ$.
$\mathrm{NH_3}$: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair → trigonal pyramidal; the lone pair squeezes the angle to $107^\circ$.
$\mathrm{H_2O}$: 2 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs → bent (V-shape); two lone pairs squeeze hardest, angle $104.5^\circ$.
Order: $\mathrm{CH_4}$ ($109.5^\circ$) > $\mathrm{NH_3}$ ($107^\circ$) > $\mathrm{H_2O}$ ($104.5^\circ$) — more lone pairs, smaller angle.

questions.question: Which has the strongest hydrogen bonding, and why? (a) $\mathrm{H_2O}$ (b) $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (c) $\mathrm{HF}$
questions.solution: (c) $\mathrm{HF}$. Hydrogen-bond strength follows the electronegativity of the atom holding H: F (4.0) > O (3.5) > N (3.0). The most polar H–X bond gives the most positive H, hence the strongest attraction to a neighbouring lone pair. (Water still boils higher than HF overall because each water molecule forms more H-bonds — a network effect.)
